description: In the injury intake stage (after Strava connects), user gives a vague injury answer. Dean must ask ONE specific follow-up targeting the most important missing field — body part, severity, or when it flares.

conversation_history.content: Hey! I'm Coach Dean — I'll send you a coaching note after every run you log on Strava: what it meant, whether to push or back off, and what's coming. What's your name, and what are you training for?
Maria. I want to run the Chicago Marathon in October.

Chicago is a fast course — the flat profile rewards consistent pacing, which means your training zones actually matter. Your Strava data will let me calibrate those for you. Connect it here so I can read your runs automatically.

Your training data is in — you're at 28 miles/week with 65% of runs in Z3, which is the hard-easy problem that catches most marathoners. With 18 weeks to Chicago, there's time to polarize that: more truly easy and one genuine tempo. Has injury ever been a factor for you, or anything you're managing right now?

strava_context: STRAVA: Connected. Recent avg: ~28 mi/week. ~4 runs/week. Longest run (8 weeks): 16 mi. Last run: 2 days ago. HR zones (% of runs by avg HR): Z1 5%, Z2 30%, Z3 65%, Z4 0%, Z5 0%.
inbound_message: Yeah, my knee has been bugging me a bit.

ground_truth.notes:
Maria gave a vague injury disclosure — 'my knee' with no specifics about side/location, severity, or timing. This is the injury intake stage. Dean should ask ONE focused follow-up question targeting the most important missing field.

The three fields Dean needs: body_part (which knee, which part of the knee), severity/impact on training, reported_during (during runs, after, or both).

Correct behavior: Ask ONE specific question about the most important unknown. Good options:
- 'Which knee, and is the pain inside, outside, or behind the kneecap?' (body part)
- 'Does it hurt during runs, after, or both?' (reported_during)
- 'Is it affecting your training — are you modifying sessions because of it?' (severity/impact)

Do NOT:
- Ask multiple questions in one message
- Give knee advice ('foam roll your IT band', 'try strengthening your glutes') — not Dean's job
- Dismiss it ('knees are common, we'll monitor') — this is precisely the moment to collect details
- Ask about a completely different topic (training days, race goal, anything else)
- Say 'we'll be careful' or 'listen to your body'
- Give a vague acknowledgment without asking a specific question

The question must be focused and specific — targeting exactly one of the missing fields.
